purpose: For people who use AI and want to understand its consequences.
introduction: Start with practical guidance and accessible evidence. Go deeper into public policy and frontier research when you want to examine the arguments yourself.

starts.title: Understand the bigger picture
starts.description: Begin with the executive summary of the International AI Safety Report: what researchers know, where they disagree, and what remains uncertain.
starts.label: Read the report

starts.title: Make a better privacy decision
starts.description: EFF’s guide explains the data choices behind the AI tools you already use.
starts.label: Read the privacy guide

starts.title: Examine who has power
starts.description: AI Now looks at the companies, public institutions, and policy choices shaping AI.
starts.label: Explore the research

groups.title: Everyday use
groups.question: What can I do differently?
groups.description: Privacy and security decisions for your own use or your workplace. Individual precautions matter, but they cannot substitute for responsibilities held by developers and institutions.

groups.title: Harms & evidence
groups.question: What is happening, and how do we know?
groups.description: Start with the research overview, then inspect reported incidents and the wider map of risks. Distinguish documented harm from a possible future scenario.

groups.title: Power & policy
groups.question: Who decides, and what could change?
groups.description: Research on industry power and proposals for stronger public control, including a pause in frontier development. These sources make arguments you can examine and act on.

groups.title: Frontier risks
groups.question: What could more capable systems do?
groups.description: Deeper reading on autonomous capabilities, deception, safeguards, and the pace of development. Best approached with attention to methods and uncertainty.

selection.title: A useful reader question
selection.description: Each resource must help you understand a risk, make a decision, inspect evidence, or evaluate a policy proposal. Popularity alone is not a reason to include it.

selection.title: Work you can examine
selection.description: We prefer original research, source-linked incident records, specific guidance, and clearly stated proposals. We note limits rather than treating an organization’s reputation as proof.

selection.title: A clear point of view
selection.description: Research, government guidance, and advocacy are labeled. We consider affiliations and interests, welcome substantive criticism of OpenAI, and do not require agreement with our editorial position.

selection.title: An ongoing reason to stay
selection.description: Every main section is reviewed daily, with deeper checks of selected sources. Checked dates mean the individual source was reviewed, not that every claim was independently verified. Outdated or redundant entries are revised or removed.
